audit: auth acquisition plan to existing native download queue
mode: read_only_source_audit; only this ignored report created
snapshot_note: Auth acquisition-plan definition landed during this audit. Hashes identify the final bytes read here; this report does not establish their compile, TLS, or native execution result. Frozen core products and tests were not modified.

current_contract.queue_capacity: Eight total process-lifetime source records shared by all browser sessions. c.count never decreases; analyzed, failed and needs-authorization records consume slots. Public counts are cookie-filtered, so they do not reveal global free capacity.
current_contract.idempotency: Current single-submit key is bound to cookie fingerprint and exact kind/game/mod/file. Identical replay returns original record; changed identity conflicts. New records are staged, serialized and finally admitted before array/count mutation. There is no acquisition-group replay receipt or atomic multi-record submit.
current_contract.ownership: Each source is owned by the submitting session cookie fingerprint; private queued cookie/CSRF/Origin are stored only until worker resolution. Every source domain is explicit. Auth active account can change; existing worker injects current private bearer and performs fresh live authorization rather than trusting prior plan or caller account claims.
current_contract.auth_call_under_job_busy: Allowed and already exercised structurally by admission and run_one: jobs and auth are separate opaque contexts with separate Busy flags. Internal auth_plan call can run under jobs Busy. Calling public jobs_submit recursively under that same guard returns BUSY; calling auth recursively while auth Busy also refuses.
current_contract.plan: The internal auth API accepts strict acquisition intent with cookie/CSRF/Origin, computes visibility/files/requirements under one operation, and emits selected_sources only when the complete bounded closure is ready. Plan remains download_authorized=false, compatibility/version_satisfaction unresolved; external/DLC/cross-game/cyclic/unknown-choice cases cannot silently produce a ready subset.
current_contract.worker: Source records are processed before queued generations. Every run_one invokes auth-owned live profile, entitlement/grant binding, mod visibility and provider link resolution; only complete final URI success reaches credential-free curl sink, inode-bound read-only reopening and unchanged archive analysis. Transient URI is erased and no plan-provided URI/headers/premium flag are accepted.
current_contract.free_account: The resolver accepts a bound expiring website grant, but jobs submit currently rejects nxm and the worker supplies no grant. Non-premium jobs reach needs_nexus_authorization before link lookup. No queued resume/grant method exists; acquisition readiness cannot bypass or solve this.
current_contract.execution_loop: host.c sends/closes the HTTP response before one synchronous run_one per accepted request. It has no background drain: additional queued sources advance on subsequent requests. Polls wait while the synchronous worker is running.
current_contract.public_authority: All existing public jobs/generations remain runtime_supported=false and installation_supported=false; source selection and successful private byte preparation do not prove version compatibility or game load order.

scope: jobs.h: one additive acquisition-submit ABI accepting original strict acquisition intent and separate bounded group idempotency key, never a serialized client plan
jobs.cpp: one internal auth-plan call plus bounded all-record staging and atomic commit; existing single-submit/worker unchanged
http.c: one dispatch to that jobs operation after existing same-origin/CSRF/session framing
host.c: retain serial owner; if autonomous completion is required, explicitly add bounded serial draining after response rather than claiming the present one-per-request loop already drains
smallest_bounded_increment.private_group_receipt: Bounded process-lifetime receipt beside existing arrays: cookie fingerprint + group key + canonical accepted intent identity + ordered selected game/mod/file/job IDs. It is a replay/admission mapping only, with no credentials, URL, private provider body or disk persistence. Keep the group namespace explicit and bound it by the eight source-slot design.
smallest_bounded_increment.replay: After local session/account/CSRF/Origin admission, check stored group receipt before provider discovery. Same accepted intent/key returns original source IDs even if a later primary file changes; changed intent/key binding conflicts. Compact receipt avoids concatenating eight potentially large analyzed public_job reports into the 98304-byte jobs output.
fresh_admission_order: Hold jobs Busy; validate layouts/aliases, strict original acquisition intent/key, exact cookie/CSRF/Origin, configured auth, storage and closing state. Refuse plan/source-list/URI/premium authority supplied by the client.

Call mb_nexus_auth_acquisition_plan_v1 on separate auth context with owned scratch and one configured operation budget. Consume only its final OK/complete output; validate exact ready schema, same game, no unresolved items, 1..8 unique chosen identities and complete closure.

For the smallest first increment do not infer reuse of unrelated prior jobs: all selected identities become new download_analyze records. Require selected_count <= 8-c.count before generating IDs or mutating records. A future explicit reuse contract can be separate; no partial implicit reuse now.

Stage every Record and the group receipt privately. Get checked entropy, reject collisions with existing source/generation IDs and with every staged ID, attach private session bindings, and render compact response before committing anything.

Release large provider/plan scratch and perform final checked deadline/cancel and auth/session/account/CSRF/Origin gates, plus storage/closing checks. Then commit all staged records/count/group receipt in one bounded non-failing section; no fallible callback, allocation, serialization or recursive public submit between first and last insertion.

Return queued child IDs, never an authorized/completed group claim. Existing worker performs independent authorization and unchanged transfer/analysis for each. Atomic admission does not imply atomic network execution; preserve individual needs-authorization/failure states and successful private originals.
smallest_bounded_increment.generation_readiness: Only after every bound child is Analyzed, downloaded, identity-valid and owns an unchanged original leaf with report/SHA/nonzero size <=512MiB, and all children have the same cookie and the explicitly configured IoStore source game. Pass exactly the receipt ordered original source IDs into existing generations submit; it snapshots bytes/SHA/base token and the worker reopens/revalidates all sources before ONE prepare_batch. Failed/missing children must prevent subset generation. Acquisition order is not load priority; existing strict overlap conflicts remain conflicts.
smallest_bounded_increment.current_generation_scope: The existing multi-source generation entrypoint is IoStore only. Do not promise a PAK/INI mixed generation or platform support from this queue connection.
smallest_bounded_increment.slots: Eight is global remaining capacity, not eight per acquisition group. Plan may be metadata-ready but cannot be admitted when earlier records fill capacity. Generations have a separate eight-record bound.

focused_next_proofs: Owned HTTP/TLS plan computes 2+ selected sources internally, admits one group, and existing real resolver/sink/archive reader processes them; client-forged plan or URI is rejected. Keep account/provider fixture provenance explicit.

Insufficient global slots, staged kth entropy failure/collision, short output and final admission/deadline failure leave zero new records, no group receipt and no archive file. Same replay returns identical child IDs; changed intent conflicts.

Non-premium/no-grant or one failed child never becomes group acquisition success or partial generation. Successful unchanged same-cookie/same-game child originals qualify the existing generation path, with exact SHA/size rebind; single-job behavior stays unchanged.
